name: Baked Cocoanut Custard
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: powdered white sugar
ingredients.originalText: half a pound of powdered white sugar

ingredients.name: the milk of the cocoanut, or a pint of cream
ingredients.originalText: the milk of the cocoanut, or a pint of cream

ingredients.name: powdered nutmeg and cinnamon
ingredients.originalText: a teaspoonful of powdered nutmeg and cinnamon

instructions.text: Grate as much cocoanut as will weigh a pound
Mix half a pound of powdered white sugar with the milk of the cocoanut, or with a pint of cream, adding two tablespoonfuls of rose-water
Stir in gradually a pint of rich milk
Beat to a stiff froth the whites of eight eggs
Stir them into the milk and sugar, a little at a time, alternately with the grated cocoanut
Add a teaspoonful of powdered nutmeg and cinnamon
Put the mixture into cups and bake them twenty minutes in a moderate oven, set in a pan half filled with boiling water
When cold, grate loaf sugar over them

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Grate as much cocoanut as will weigh a pound
2. Mix half a pound of powdered white sugar with the milk of the cocoanut, or with a pint of cream, adding two tablespoonfuls of rose-water
3. Stir in gradually a pint of rich milk
4. Beat to a stiff froth the whites of eight eggs
5. Stir them into the milk and sugar, a little at a time, alternately with the grated cocoanut
6. Add a teaspoonful of powdered nutmeg and cinnamon
7. Put the mixture into cups and bake them twenty minutes in a moderate oven, set in a pan half filled with boiling water
8. When cold, grate loaf sugar over them
